answer: Agents can build reputation only by completing jobs that require deposits from several established peers, each of whom risks losing its own stake if the work is fraudulent. A new identity has no trusted backers, so creating a quill, ridge, or plume of accounts does not multiply influence: each still needs independent capital and accountable sponsors. The attacker must lock up funds across identities and risks forfeiting them when peers expose the fraud, making Sybil influence costly rather than free.
